# i3blocks: a user-defined family, generated by a language override

An i3 status bar whose blocks are a SNGL tree. Run with `--window`, the same
process also opens a GTK or Fyne window that shows what the bar shows. It
compiles and runs:

```sh
sngl build --lang go --platform gtk4 --opt name=i3blocks-demo -o ~/bin bar.sngl
```

then, in `~/.config/i3/config`, `bar { status_command ~/bin/i3blocks-demo }`.
By hand, `go tool sngl run --platform gtk4 ./example/i3blocks -- --window`
prints the status lines and opens the window.

It lives under `example/` rather than `examples/` because `docsgen` loads every
`examples/*/*.sngl` into the playground, which has no Go host.

## What it demonstrates

- `bar.sngl` is the program: state, a timer, an `i3.bar` of blocks whose props
  read that state and whose `@click`s write it, and a window that `@run`
  presents only when asked to.
- `i3/i3.sngl` declares the family (`block`), its members (`text`, `gap`) and the
  root member that hosts them (`bar`).
- `i3/protocol.sngl` is the i3bar protocol in SNGL: the `Entry` each block
  contributes, `encode` from the entries to one status line, and `clickField`
  reading a click object.
- `i3/go.sngl` is `block[go.language]`, the family's generator for Go, and each
  member's `gen.node`. Its natives are the whole of the Go it names:
  `bufio.Scanner` over stdin, `fmt.Print`, `os.Exit`.

No platform is involved. gtk4 and fyne both pick the language override, and
each compiles what it becomes the way it compiles any other SNGL.

## How it is generated

`gen.emit(render=encode, @start(members) { … }, @change(line) { … })` is code
mode. The build rewrites the `bar` into SNGL before anything else sees it:

- a function returning each block's `Entry` -- the `for` over `workspaces`
  kept as written, each block's `gen.node(value=Entry{…})` with its props bound,
  and each block's `@click` a closure the entry carries;
- in the bar's place, the family's `gen.emit`, handed that function. It is an
  ordinary component of `sngl:x/gen`: one effect mounted at start, which writes
  the header and starts the click reader, and one keyed on
  `encode(members())`, which prints the line each time it differs.

So a state write re-renders the bar because an effect's key read that state, and
a click is a closure posted to the drawing thread with `async.post`. Neither host
has any code for i3.

## Not yet

- **A window under a reactive `if`** (`if details { ui.window … }`) and a
  window's `@close` writing its condition back: Phase C of `SNGL_PLUGINS.md`.
  Here `details` shows and hides part of one window instead.
- **The header before the host starts.** It is written by `@start`, which
  runs with the tree's first settle -- once the host has built the tree and
  before `@run`. Nothing here needs it earlier; an emitter's own layer of the
  process start (`p.main` in `SNGL_PLUGINS.md`) is what would.
- **One line per handler.** The effect settles after every write, so a tick
  writing `uptime` and then `samples` prints two lines. i3bar shows the last,
  but the protocol carries both.
